name: God Object
description: A God Object is a class that knows or does too much. It centralizes too much responsibility, leading to a complex, tightly coupled system that is hard to maintain and understand. This often violates the Single Responsibility Principle and the principle of Separation of Concerns.

cppExamples.title: Before Refactoring: Monolithic System Class
cppExamples.explanation: The `SmartHomeSystem` class manages user authentication, device control (lights, thermostat, security), and scheduling. Any change to one aspect (e.g., adding a new device type) requires modifying this large class, increasing risk and complexity.

cppExamples.title: After Refactoring: Delegated Responsibilities
cppExamples.explanation: Responsibilities are delegated to specialized classes: `UserManager`, `LightManager`, `ThermostatManager`, `SecurityManager`, and `Scheduler`. The `SmartHomeSystem` now acts as a coordinator, simplifying its role and making the system more modular.

refactoringTechniques.name: Extract Class
refactoringTechniques.description: Identify distinct responsibilities within the God Object and move them into separate classes. This is the primary method for breaking down a God Object.

refactoringTechniques.name: Delegate Responsibility
refactoringTechniques.description: Modify the God Object to delegate tasks to the new, smaller classes it now collaborates with.

refactoringTechniques.name: Identify and Separate Concerns
refactoringTechniques.description: Analyze the God Object to find different areas of concern (e.g., user management, data processing, UI handling) and separate them into their own modules or classes.
